claims.text: The starting material consists of W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix.
Optimized spark plasma sintering can produce a uniform W-Cu composite.
The proposed SPS temperature range is 1000-1200 °C.
The proposed SPS pressure range is 50-100 MPa.
The proposed SPS holding-time range is 30-60 minutes.
The SPS intervention will produce a uniform distribution of W particles in the Cu matrix.
Diffusion and consolidation of the W and Cu phases occur during SPS and provide the proposed mechanism.
The optimized SPS composite will have 20-30% higher thermal conductivity than a conventionally induction- or arc-plasma-cast material.
The optimized SPS composite will have 10-20% higher mechanical strength than a conventionally induction- or arc-plasma-cast material.
The proposed material is intended to operate from 500 to 1000 °C.
The proposed material is intended to tolerate irradiation doses from 10 to 100 dpa.
Residual porosity or defects may remain after optimized SPS.

contradictions.description: Mechanical-strength gains of 10% to less than 15% satisfy the predicted 10-20% range but would also fall below the stated 15% falsification threshold. Thus, part of the predicted outcome is classified as falsifying.
